scoreMeaning: Subjective /10 craft judgment of the current static GitHub application, not a precise measurement, audience result or website score. Fresh scope; not a numerical continuation of my prior 8.8 gesture/staging judgment.
confidence: High for shown static palette, proportions and desktop/narrow composition; moderate for small-detail reading beyond these rasterized captures. Manifest verification supports provenance, not human response.
strengths: Both 1440px captures retain a cream face as the character's lightest focal mass, quiet wing planes and an oversized head above a compact body. The header preserves all four wings and attached feet; the avatar is a head crop, not altered anatomy.

The light chartreuse ground becomes the dark header's chartreuse wordmark against forest. The warmer night cream still belongs to the same palette. Native blue links remain visually functional, while brand color stays concentrated in the identity art.

The universal paper-ground avatar preserves the face and unequal antenna paddles in both 320px top captures. The 238px-wide header still clearly carries heyNag and a small whole character; its meaning does not require reading the mittens.

Actual scrolled README and pin captures show calm native text, useful project descriptions and no decorative interruption. Nag's name and first-person introduction keep authorship explicit beside the companion.

deductions.issue: Night antenna stems have a more delicate, doubled-edge reading than the solid day contour; at narrow banner scale they are weaker than the bright paddles and face.
deductions.improvementCriterion: Any optional paint-only experiment must improve stem continuity at the actual 238px banner width while preserving paddles, geometry, quiet cream and day/night identity. Do not add glow or enlarge anatomy merely to chase a score.

deductions.issue: At 320px the full-body character's ruff and mitten detail condense into a dense small cluster. The face and silhouette work better than the fine material separation.
deductions.improvementCriterion: If stronger gesture or material legibility becomes a requirement, compare an application-scale composition variant in both themes. Adopt only demonstrated separation with the tiny proportions intact; no current message depends on this detail.

deductions.issue: The large pale avatar disk creates a stronger isolated light mass on dark desktop than the warmer header face. This makes dark-theme integration less seamless than light-theme integration.
deductions.improvementCriterion: Retain the dependable universal avatar unless a reversible ground-only comparison improves desktop integration and preserves small-avatar contrast in both themes. A separate night account avatar is not a solution to GitHub's single-avatar constraint.

recommendations: Keep the present paired static headers and universal day avatar as the current profile treatment; preserve original raster, source geometry and native readable text.

Carry a versioned source and explicit surface-color mapping into the future website. The application dark ground is #202B21, while CSS ink is #1C1C1C and functional forest is #36552D; related greens are not interchangeable tokens by accident.
Treat narrow fine-detail experiments as optional improvements with named benefits. Do not introduce grain, stronger glow, enlarged hands or compulsory animation.
continuityAssessment: The shown profile provides a coherent visual starting point: the same face, unequal paddles, chartreuse, cream and ink support both themes. continuity.json sensibly preserves source, proportions, useful work and a quiet path. Its statement that recognition is established immediately is a design intention, not demonstrated human recognition. The website has no rendered opening to assess; reuse of assets alone will not prove its scale, material integration or hierarchy.
unscoredOutcomes: Built website quality, responsive website behavior and cross-surface human recognition.
